role: Agentic-first distributed version control; a Git replacement with pluggable content types beyond source code.

capabilities.name: repo.read
capabilities.description: Inspect without changing anything: log, diff, status, show, search, verify. The 20 commands Lit declares `safe`.

capabilities.name: repo.write
capabilities.description: Record new history: commit, add, snapshot, tag, branch creation. Creates objects and moves refs, but supersedes nothing.

capabilities.name: repo.rewrite
capabilities.description: Change what history says: reset, revert, stash, merge, conflict resolution. Six of the eight history commands are declared unsafe, and these are the ones that can discard work an agent did not create.

capabilities.name: repo.collaborate
capabilities.description: Exchange with a remote: push, pull, clone. The only capability here that leaves the machine, which makes it the one where a mistake becomes someone else's.

capabilities.name: repo.maintain
capabilities.description: Garbage collection and LFS migration. Reclaims space by deleting what it judges unreachable, so it is destructive in a way that reads as routine.

capabilities.name: repo.interop
capabilities.description: Import from or export to Git. Both declared unsafe: each writes a whole repository.

capabilities.name: security.rotate_key
capabilities.description: Rotate the encryption key. One command, declared unsafe, and the one whose failure mode is losing access to the repository rather than corrupting it.

capabilities.name: swarm.coordinate
capabilities.description: Register an agent, acquire and release file leases. How concurrent agents avoid working over each other.

capabilities.name: server.serve
capabilities.description: Run the REST or MCP server. Declared unsafe because it exposes the repository to whatever can reach the port.

note: requires_grant is not hand-assigned: it follows the `safe` flag Lit already publishes for each of its 48 commands in `lit ontology --json`. Capabilities group those commands by what kind of authority they need, so this manifest and the ontology are derived from one source rather than maintained twice. Nothing is budgeted, deliberately: no operation here scales with a caller-supplied quantity, and the risk is an unauthorised rewrite rather than too many of them — a budget on `reset` would let the first one through, which is the one that matters.
